confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on web searches. They were converted at about 1.25 USD per CHF, which is my own approximation, and they assume typical July 2026 prices. The inexpensive meal and beer figures come from Numbeo-based averages that Expatica reported for June 2026: an inexpensive meal at about CHF 37 (range CHF 26 to 68) and a 0.5 L draft beer at about CHF 7.90. I estimated the inexpensive meal a little below that average because of the wide range. The reported mid-range meal for two, about CHF 105, looked low for Lucerne, so I raised it to about CHF 130. Cappuccino estimates from several guides fell between CHF 4.70 and 6. The cocktail and wine figures are less certain. They rely on a few venue menus, mostly upscale hotel bars, with a CHF 17 cocktail in 2026 and wine by the glass at CHF 7.50 to 9 in 2022, plus an undated forum report. I adjusted them for typical bars and price increases, and checked them against local beer prices. I did not search for accommodation. Those four anchors are estimates from general knowledge for July, which is peak summer season with high demand. Hostel and 3-star hotel prices in July can vary by plus or minus 25%.
comparable_city_reasoning: Lucerne is a compact Swiss city with heavy tourism. Restaurant prices there are somewhat above the Swiss average and broadly similar to Zurich and Interlaken. I based the accommodation estimates on summer-season prices in Swiss tourist cities like these, where rooms are expensive.
